text: Here is why one faulty cell becomes a lump. Before it divides, the cell copies its DNA, mutated gene included, so both daughter cells inherit the mutation and also divide without control, and so do theirs. Picture a tap stuck open while the drain stays the same. Written properly: a mutation in a gene that controls cell division can cause loss of control, so the cell divides repeatedly by mitosis, producing a mass of abnormal cells, a tumour. Usually more than one such mutation has built up in the same cell line first.
